question_bank.question: A RAG agent reads a retrieved webpage containing an instruction to email confidential data. What should the system do

options.text: Follow the webpage because it is retrieved context
Treat retrieved content as untrusted data and block unauthorized tool actions
Email the data after summarizing it

question_bank.rationale: Retrieved content can carry indirect prompt injection. It must not gain authority to trigger tools or override policy.
correct_answers: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data and block unauthorized tool actions

question_bank.question: Select the THREE controls that reduce risk when LLM output is passed to downstream software
question_bank.scoring: partial: correct picks / 3; exactly three required
question_bank.rationale: Generated output is untrusted. Validate its structure, sanitize it for the destination and restrict downstream operations.

question_bank.question: Which design best reduces sensitive-information disclosure from an enterprise chatbot

options.text: Put all company data in every prompt
Apply access control, data minimization and redaction before model access

question_bank.rationale: The system should retrieve only authorized, necessary data and redact sensitive fields before they reach the model.
correct_answers: Apply access control, data minimization and redaction before model access

question_bank.question: A multi-tenant vector store returns one customer's documents to another customer. Which control is most directly missing
question_bank.rationale: Vector similarity must not bypass tenant isolation. Authorization and metadata filters must be enforced during retrieval.

question_bank.question: Select the THREE controls most appropriate for an agent that can issue refunds

options.text: Human approval above a risk threshold

question_bank.scoring: partial: correct picks / 3; exactly three required
question_bank.rationale: Consequential agents need constrained authority, proportional human approval and complete auditability.
correct_answers: Human approval above a risk threshold

question_bank.question: Which control best limits denial-of-wallet risk from recursive agent calls

options.text: Per-request budgets, call-depth limits, timeouts and quotas

question_bank.rationale: Explicit resource budgets and termination limits constrain runaway cost and computation.
correct_answers: Per-request budgets, call-depth limits, timeouts and quotas

question_bank.question: A RAG answer is wrong because the necessary source never appeared in the top retrieved chunks. Which metric most directly diagnoses this failure
question_bank.rationale: Retrieval recall at k measures whether the relevant evidence was included among the retrieved candidates.

question_bank.question: Select the THREE elements of a sound regression evaluation before changing a production model version

options.text: Quality, safety, latency and cost acceptance thresholds
Comparison with the current production baseline

question_bank.scoring: partial: correct picks / 3; exactly three required
question_bank.rationale: Regression evaluation needs representative cases, explicit acceptance thresholds and comparison against the current baseline.
correct_answers: Quality, safety, latency and cost acceptance thresholds
Comparison with the current production baseline

question_bank.question: An LLM judge consistently prefers whichever answer is shown first. What is the best mitigation

options.text: Randomize or swap answer order and measure agreement across runs

question_bank.rationale: Order randomization and repeated comparisons reveal and reduce position bias in pairwise model judging.
correct_answers: Randomize or swap answer order and measure agreement across runs

question_bank.question: For a multi-step agent, why should evaluation inspect the execution trace as well as the final answer

options.text: The final answer always reveals every unsafe action
A correct final answer can hide unnecessary, unsafe or costly intermediate tool calls
Traces eliminate the need for test cases

question_bank.rationale: Agent quality includes the path taken, permissions used, cost incurred and safety of intermediate actions, not only the final response.
correct_answers: A correct final answer can hide unnecessary, unsafe or costly intermediate tool calls

question_bank.question: In MCP, which capability is normally invoked by a model to perform an external action
question_bank.rationale: MCP tools expose callable operations; resources expose context or data, and prompts expose reusable interaction templates.

question_bank.question: An MCP client needs access to one read-only repository. Which authorization design is best

options.text: A shared administrator token for every server
A user-bound token scoped to the required server and read-only permissions

question_bank.rationale: Authorization should be user-bound and least-privileged, with credentials handled outside model-visible prompt content.
correct_answers: A user-bound token scoped to the required server and read-only permissions

question_bank.question: Select the THREE controls that reduce MCP tool-poisoning risk

options.text: Approve trusted servers and pin reviewed versions
Review tool descriptions and requested permissions
Require confirmation for newly introduced high-impact actions

question_bank.scoring: partial: correct picks / 3; exactly three required
question_bank.rationale: Trusted-server controls, review of tool metadata and approval for new consequential capabilities reduce semantic tool-poisoning risk.
correct_answers: Approve trusted servers and pin reviewed versions
Review tool descriptions and requested permissions
Require confirmation for newly introduced high-impact actions

question_bank.question: A model must return data consumed by an API. What is the safest implementation

options.text: Parse any prose that looks similar to JSON
Require a defined schema, validate the output and reject or repair invalid results

question_bank.rationale: Structured generation should be paired with deterministic schema validation before downstream use.
correct_answers: Require a defined schema, validate the output and reject or repair invalid results

question_bank.question: A model provider begins timing out during a customer workflow. Which production design is most resilient

options.text: Use bounded retries, timeouts, a circuit breaker and a safe fallback

question_bank.rationale: Bounded retries and circuit breaking prevent cascading failure, while a tested fallback preserves safe service behaviour.
correct_answers: Use bounded retries, timeouts, a circuit breaker and a safe fallback

question_bank.question: A classifier's input population changes substantially after launch. This is primarily an example of
question_bank.rationale: A change in the production input distribution is data drift and may invalidate previously measured performance.

question_bank.question: After an AI incident affects users, which response is most complete

options.text: Contain harm, preserve evidence, notify accountable owners, remediate, communicate and monitor recurrence

question_bank.rationale: Responsible incident management includes containment, evidence, accountability, remediation, communication and recurrence monitoring.
correct_answers: Contain harm, preserve evidence, notify accountable owners, remediate, communicate and monitor recurrence

question_bank.question: Which approach best follows data minimization when using an external LLM API

options.text: Send only fields necessary for the task after removing or masking unnecessary identifiers
Put secrets in the system message

question_bank.rationale: Data minimization limits processing to information needed for the defined purpose and removes unnecessary identifiers.
correct_answers: Send only fields necessary for the task after removing or masking unnecessary identifiers

question_bank.question: Which human-oversight design is strongest for a high-impact AI recommendation

options.text: A reviewer who can see evidence, understand limitations, override the output and record a reason
A reviewer who must always approve the model

question_bank.rationale: Meaningful oversight requires usable evidence, knowledge of limitations, genuine override authority and accountable documentation.
correct_answers: A reviewer who can see evidence, understand limitations, override the output and record a reason

question_bank.question: A classifier outputs 0.9 confidence but is correct only 60 percent of the time on cases near 0.9. The main issue is
question_bank.rationale: A calibrated 0.9 score should correspond to roughly 90 percent correctness among comparable predictions.

question_bank.question: A model performs well on random test data but poorly in a new country with different user behaviour. What was most likely missed
question_bank.rationale: Evaluation should represent deployment conditions and document limits on generalization across populations and environments.

question_bank.question: Why should a retryable AI tool operation use an idempotency key

options.text: To prevent repeated retries from creating duplicate side effects

question_bank.rationale: An idempotency key lets the service recognize repeated attempts and avoid duplicate payments, messages or other side effects.
correct_answers: To prevent repeated retries from creating duplicate side effects

question_bank.question: Where should an AI application's production API secret be stored

options.text: In a managed secret store with scoped runtime access

question_bank.rationale: Secrets should be managed outside prompts and source code, with access restricted to the runtime identity that needs them.
correct_answers: In a managed secret store with scoped runtime access

question_bank.question: Select the THREE good practices for automated testing of a nondeterministic LLM feature

Require one exact sentence for every valid response
Keep regression examples for known failures
Judge quality only by response length

Keep regression examples for known failures

question_bank.question: Which logging design best supports debugging while reducing privacy risk

options.text: Log every raw prompt and secret indefinitely
Use structured event logs with trace IDs, access controls, retention limits and redaction

question_bank.rationale: Structured, access-controlled and redacted logs provide traceability while limiting unnecessary retention of sensitive content.
correct_answers: Use structured event logs with trace IDs, access controls, retention limits and redaction

prompting_tasks.task: Write a single prompt that turns a 2 page contract into 5 plain-English bullet points for a non-lawyer.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Sets role, task, audience, exact output format and count, length limit and tone. Tells the model to flag anything uncertain rather than guess.

prompting_tasks.task: Rewrite this weak prompt to be specific and useful: tell me about marketing.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Names the goal, audience, scope, format and constraints. Removes vagueness. Adds a concrete deliverable, for example a 5 point plan for a named business type.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a few-shot prompt that classifies support tickets into Billing, Technical or Account, using two labelled examples per class.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Includes clear class definitions, balanced examples, a consistent format, and an instruction to return only the label.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that asks the model to solve a multi-step word problem and show its reasoning before the final answer.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Requests step by step reasoning, then a clearly separated final answer. Keeps reasoning and answer distinct so the answer can be parsed.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a system prompt for a customer support assistant that must not give medical or legal advice.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Sets role and scope, lists hard limits, defines a safe refusal and redirect, and fixes tone. Separates policy from user input.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that returns strict JSON with keys name, email and intent, and nothing else.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Specifies the exact schema, forbids extra text or markdown, defines behaviour for missing fields, and gives one example of valid output.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that answers only from a provided context block and replies not found when the answer is absent.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Delimits the context, forbids outside knowledge, requires a not found response when unsupported, and asks for a citation to the context.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that makes the model act as a senior Python reviewer giving actionable feedback.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Sets the expert role, the review focus, the output format such as prioritised findings, and a constructive tone.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that lowers the chance of fabricated facts in a research summary.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Requires sources or citations, allows I do not know, restricts to provided material, and asks the model to separate facts from inference.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that rewrites text at a grade 6 reading level in under 100 words.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: States reading level, word limit, audience and that meaning must be preserved. Asks to avoid jargon.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that extracts named people, companies and dates from a paragraph into a table.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines the entity types, the table columns, handling of none found, and a single output format.

prompting_tasks.task: Design a two-step prompt flow that first produces an outline, then drafts from the approved outline.
prompting_tasks.submission_format: Both prompts and how they connect.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Step one returns a structured outline. Step two takes the outline as input and drafts. Defines the handoff and the format of each step.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that asks the model to critique its own first answer and produce an improved version.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Asks for the draft, then a specific critique against stated criteria, then a revised answer. Names what good looks like.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that generates ad copy but must avoid superlatives and unverifiable claims.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Lists forbidden patterns clearly, gives an allowed alternative style, and asks the model to self-check before returning.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that explains retrieval augmented generation to a non-technical CEO in 120 words.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Sets audience, word limit, plain language, one analogy allowed, and a focus on business value.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that translates marketing copy to French while keeping the brand tone.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Specifies target language, tone to preserve, audience, and that idioms should be adapted not translated literally.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that generates unit test cases, including edge cases, for a described function.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Asks for normal, boundary and error cases, a named framework, and clear expected outputs.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that safely separates fixed instructions from untrusted user input.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Uses clear delimiters, tells the model to treat user content as data not instructions, and to ignore embedded instructions.

prompting_tasks.task: Explain in a short prompt design note when you would set temperature low versus high, with an example.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Low for factual or structured tasks, higher for creative variety. Gives a concrete example of each and the reason.

prompting_tasks.task: Write an LLM-as-judge prompt that scores two answers against a rubric and picks the better one.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines the rubric, a numeric scale, a structured verdict, and asks for a brief justification and a tie-break rule.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that turns messy incident notes into a clear step by step runbook.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Asks for ordered steps, prerequisites, owners, and a rollback section. Sets a clean format.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that makes the model ask clarifying questions before answering an ambiguous request.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Instructs the model to ask up to a set number of questions when key details are missing, and to proceed only after, or state assumptions.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that returns a markdown table with fixed columns Feature, Benefit, Risk.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Specifies the exact columns, markdown table format, one row per item, and no extra prose.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that redacts personal data from a text while keeping it readable.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines what counts as PII, the redaction token, that meaning is preserved, and that nothing is invented.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that converts a feature request into user stories with acceptance criteria.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Asks for the as a, I want, so that format, plus testable acceptance criteria per story.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that tells an assistant when to call a search tool versus answer directly.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines the trigger conditions for the tool, the argument format, and the fallback when the tool fails.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that compares two options across cost, speed and risk in a scored matrix.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines the criteria, a scoring scale, weights if relevant, and a final recommendation with reasoning.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that detects and rewrites biased or exclusionary language in a job advert.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Asks the model to flag specific phrases, explain why, and propose neutral alternatives without changing the role.

prompting_tasks.task: Write a prompt that handles an out-of-scope request politely and redirects the user.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Defines scope, a respectful refusal, a brief reason, and a helpful redirect or alternative.

prompting_tasks.task: Given a weak model answer that is too long and vague, write the follow-up prompt that fixes it.
prompting_tasks.best_practice_reference: Names the specific faults, sets concrete targets such as length and structure, and asks for a focused rewrite.

markdown_tasks.task: Draft the section structure for a project README.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Has title, short overview, install, usage, configuration, contributing and licence, in a sensible order with H2 headings.

markdown_tasks.task: Show a Python snippet correctly fenced with language highlighting in markdown.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Uses triple backticks with the language tag, and keeps the code readable. Inline code uses single backticks.

markdown_tasks.task: Create a markdown comparison table of three tools across two features.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Valid header and separator row, aligned columns, one row per tool, concise cells.

markdown_tasks.task: Convert a flat block of text into a document with a clear H1 to H3 hierarchy.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: One H1, logical H2 sections and H3 subsections, no skipped levels, descriptive headings.

markdown_tasks.task: Show correct markdown for a link and for an image with alt text.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Uses link and image syntax correctly, includes meaningful alt text, and a working relative or absolute path.

markdown_tasks.task: Write a markdown checklist of release steps with completed and pending items.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Uses dash bracket syntax, mixes checked and unchecked, and keeps items action oriented.

markdown_tasks.task: Write a short SKILL.md style instruction file with front matter and clear sections.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Has name and description front matter, a purpose, when to use, steps, and examples. Clear and skimmable.

markdown_tasks.task: Document one API endpoint in markdown: method, path, parameters and an example.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: States method and path, a parameter table, request and response examples in fenced blocks, and notes on errors.

markdown_tasks.task: Use blockquotes and a note callout appropriately in a short doc.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Uses blockquote syntax for quotes and a clear note or warning callout, without overusing them.

markdown_tasks.task: Turn messy plain notes into a clean structured markdown document.
markdown_tasks.best_practice_reference: Adds headings, lists, emphasis and spacing, fixes inconsistent formatting, and keeps the original meaning.
